title: SQL Managed Instance: what it buys over the database service

videos.script: Lesson 8 moved one database to Azure. Most companies do not have one database. They have an instance. {{instance}} An instance of SQL Server holds many databases. A report joins two of them. A job in SQL Agent sums the day at three in the morning. Azure SQL Database has none of that. {{habits}} SQL Managed Instance rents you the whole instance, still patched and backed up by Microsoft. {{rent}} You will practise both habits on the SQL Server in your container, which is a whole instance too. A query in one database reads a table in another. A job of five procedures sums three hundred and forty-eight days of orders. {{practice}} Then the network. An instance lives inside your own virtual network, in a subnet given over to it. {{network}} And the price, and the three roads a company takes out of the cupboard. The last question is the honest one. Is it cheaper to keep the habits, or to rewrite them? {{choice}}
